title: How to Lower Your IP Risk Score: A Practical Checklist
author: IP Ready
excerpt: Most of what moves a risk score is under your control. A pre-flight checklist, the fixes that actually work, and the rituals that waste time.
body:
A high risk score is not a life sentence. Most of the signals behind it are external facts you can work around — and a surprising number are habits you can fix in an afternoon. This is the checklist we recommend, in the order that matters.

The Pre-Flight Checklist

  • Run a scan before the session that matters — not after something breaks. The report is a rehearsal of what a platform will see.
  • Read the flagged signals, not just the number — a 45 from a stale blacklist entry and a 45 from a datacenter ASN need opposite fixes.
  • Check the blacklists yourself — if the address is listed, confirm whether the entry is current or a leftover from the address's previous life.
  • Confirm the basics agree — timezone, language, and location signals should tell the same story as the IP's registered geography.
  • Re-scan after every change — one variable at a time, so you know what moved the number.

Fixes That Actually Move the Score

Change the exit type before you change the exit. If the report shows a hosting ASN, no amount of waiting will make the address residential. Moving the account to a static residential line is the single highest-leverage fix for most people.

Replace, do not rehabilitate, heavily listed addresses. An IP with a dense recent-abuse history carries a file. Reputation can recover over months of clean behavior, but accounts rarely have that timeline — a fresh, clean address is usually the better trade.

Keep one exit per identity. The fastest way to burn a good IP is to share it across accounts that should not know each other. Isolation preserves the consistency that makes residential addresses valuable in the first place.

What Does Not Work

Clearing cookies changes your browser, not your IP's reputation — the platform saw the address, not the jar. Scanning repeatedly from the same flagged exit does not reset anything; reputation updates on the database side, on its own schedule. And hopping between VPN locations mid-session does not dilute suspicion, it manufactures location inconsistency — a new signal where none existed.

The loop is short: scan, read, change one thing, scan again. Do it before the platform becomes the one doing the testing.
